**The meaning of the verses**
﴿وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ لِأَمَانَاتِهِمْ وَعَهْدِهِمْ رَاعُونَ﴾
And those who take care of everything they have been entrusted with and fulfil all their promises.

﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَأْمُرُكُمْ أَن تُؤَدُّوا الْأَمَانَاتِ إِلَىٰ أَهْلِهَا﴾
Allah the Exalted commands you to give back the various trusts you have been entrusted with to their owners, and not to neglect them, … Allah the Exalted is All-Hearing of your words, aware of all your deeds, All-Seeing of them.

📖 At-Tafsir Al-Muyassar — King Fahd Complex.

**Talk with your child**
1. Ghaith promised to give the pencil back the next day. So why was he late? And what did he say every time he saw it in his bag?
2. What did Ghaith understand when he found that Yahya had taken his eraser and not given it back? And how did Mu'adh feel as he looked at his box?
3. Is it enough for the borrower to give the thing back, even after a month? (No; a borrowed thing is a trust: it is given back on time and unharmed, and it is not used for anything its owner did not allow. Ghaith had started drawing with it at home without permission.)

**This week's exercise**
Your child gathers everything they have that belongs to others (a library book, a friend's toy, or a classmate's pencil) and gives it all back this week. And they get used to writing down on a piece of paper what they borrow and when they will give it back, just as Ghaith began writing on his hand.
